card.name: Setapa
card.tagline: Bangwaketse harvest dance of stamping, tapping feet
card.profile: Setapa is a traditional dance of the Bangwaketse tribe of Kanye and surrounding villages in southern Botswana, its name derived from the Setswana "go tapa-tapa," to step into the ground continuously (Wikipedia; Taste of Southern Africa). Performed by mixed groups in animal-skin costume (men in motseto briefs, women in diphaeyana skirts) with ankle rattles and oxhide sandals, it features intricate tapping footwork; variants include setapa sa dipitse (galloping-horse sound) and setapa sa go goga maoto (dragging feet). It celebrates the harvest season, letlhafula.
card.insight: Setapa is a celebratory harvest dance historically performed in all-night sessions in the fields and at the village kgotla; once a gendered form where girls sang and boys danced, today both men and women take part, and it has become widely performed across Tswana-speaking communities of southern Africa (Taste of Southern Africa).
card.image_significance: Tswana continuous-footwork dance. A representative image shows drum-driven communal movement, often in a circle with vivid textiles — Tswana (Bangwaketse), Botswana.
